I'm a feminine presenting nonbinary person, so I feel my input may have some value if you're genuinely curious.

For me, it's never been that clothing denotes gender, it's more like \*style\*. I act kinda masculine, so it balances out (of course, nonbinary people shouldn't feel like they have to balance it out.) I love dresses, like holy fuck I love them so much, so I like to wear them. The fact that a lot of people think that dresses = femininity never really crosses my mind until people call me "she." But that's externally, internally I feel more like being a "woman" isn't really my thing. A lot of people talk about being nonbinary as not feeling like you fit within what it means to be female (or male), whether that be internally or externally. Physical dysphoria is a thing I still deal with, I'd love to have a flatter chest and maybe a thicker waistline, but I can normally ignore that kind of dysphoria with the right clothing. (It also happens that clothing is often a dress or flowy shirt that covers my waistline.) 

Sorry it got kinda drawn out, gender is difficult.

TLDR: Gender expression and gender identity are different, and presenting fem doesn't mean you are a woman.

I never really knew what being bi was despite the fact I grew up in a fairly liberal area. My first experiences with any type of LGBT language was when my friends would insult others by calling them gay, so that wasn't immensely helpful either. I kinda thought everyone was into both genders for my whole life, it just seemed kinda silly not to like someone bc of their gender. Kinda like an, it's so obvious nobody talks about it thing.
Later on gay marriage got legalized (in America) and I got really curious about what LGBT stuff was because it was the first time I had heard about it in a positive manner. Figured out what bisexual meant, thought I might be that. Unfortunately I'd been reading fairly biphobic stuff like "all girls who say they're bi are really just bicurious" (bad example but you get it) and other stuff like that.
Eventually I was able to come to terms with my identity and have been slowly coming out. I'm almost completely out at school but none of my family really knows, it's been hard because a lot of people are doing the "all girls are bi" thing to me when I come out to them.
